summary: N1 noise_floor() test-retests answer-span ACTIVATION NORM (predictor input), not judged E0 rate/marker logP; behavior-AGNOSTIC floor breaks plan 4.3/6 per-behavior reliability + the saturation guard.
evidence: scripts/issue658_fit_predictors.py:389-427 noise_floor() reads s[0].float().norm(dim=-1).mean() (the answer-span activation norm at the first capture layer) and test-retests THAT, returning {col: p95 for col in columns} — one shared scalar for every behavior. Plan 4.3 N1 + 6 require re-estimating E0(C,B) itself (the judged rate / marker logP — the predictor TARGET) from 8 independent 48-probe redraws, per behavior. Consequences: (1) the floor is behavior-agnostic so saturated/floored columns (refusal, harmful_compliance at theta0) do NOT get the high reliability ceiling plan 8 risk-1 relies on to suppress a false PASS; (2) the A1 gate a32_pass = best_rho(pred E0, meas E0) > noise_floor_p95 compares a predictor rho against an activation-norm test-retest rho — different quantities, so a predictor can clear the wrong floor and manufacture a false PASS in exactly the saturation regime. Fix off-pod (zero GPU): redraw the per-(C,probe) judged labels / marker logp the E0 table already stores, split-half per behavior, test-retest the per-behavior E0 estimate. Fixable before the production fit read — does not block the GPU extraction.
